title: The trim bound pinned: a 2.2 mm move is sewn across, a 2.33 mm move is trimmed
description: Five 5 x 5 mm red fill squares with gaps of 1.0, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 mm: PE-DESIGN 11.50 sews the 1.0 mm gap (a 2.2 mm needle-to-needle move) across as a plain stitch and trims the other three (2.33, 2.42 and 2.51 mm moves), so the bound lies between 2.2 and 2.33 mm; OpenStitch sews across up to 2.25 mm. The squares' y position is OpenStitch's choice. OpenStitch's optimized exit and entry points lie on the squares' edges where PE-DESIGN's lie 0.5 mm inside them and 1 mm apart in y (its moves are sqrt((gap + 1)^2 + 1) mm), so the squares are drawn at PE-DESIGN's needle-to-needle moves and the trimming rule is compared at equal moves; where PE puts its exit and entry inside the edge is the fill track's open item.

evidence.note: PE-DESIGN 11.50 reference machine/machine-trim-fine.pes (pe-refs-3, 2026-10-28): 428 stitches, 3 trims on moves of 2.33, 2.42 and 2.51 mm; the 1.0 mm gap (2.2 mm move) a plain stitch.

references.make: Import an SVG (100 x 100 mm) with five 5 x 5 mm red squares at x = 10, 16.0, 22.1, 28.3, 34.6 mm (gaps 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 mm), as Fill Stitch at PE-DESIGN's import defaults (multi-needle machine type, Jump Stitch Trimming on); change nothing. Save with Save As as PES (PE-DESIGN 11's default PES version) under the file name given, and record the PE-DESIGN version, the date, the operating system and every setting you changed in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md).

measurements.evidence: every interior move is a trimmed jump (as many moves as trims); a gap PE-DESIGN does not trim is sewn across as a stitch, never left as a plain jump
PE-DESIGN's count (its fill rows join differently from OpenStitch's, the text-fill item of the audit)
